Aapravasi Ghat is the immigration depot at Port Louis where about 450,000 indentured labourers, most of them from India, landed between 1834 and 1920.

After slavery ended, Mauritius was the first colony where the British tried indentured labour on a large scale, the so-called great experiment. Workers signed contracts for years of work on the sugar estates, and the system was then copied in the Caribbean, Fiji and Natal.

Their descendants now form about two thirds of the population and have led the country since independence under Seewoosagur Ramgoolam. The site was listed by UNESCO in 2006 as a memorial of the indenture system.
